trigger_code:
import re

def check_rule(text: str):
    lines = [ln.strip() for ln in text.splitlines()]
    nonempty = [ln for ln in lines if ln]
    if not nonempty:
        return [{'reason': 'missing title'}]
    title = nonempty[0]
    if title.startswith('#'):
        title = re.sub(r'^#{1,6}\s*', '', title).strip()
    words = title.split()
    sentence_like = bool(re.search(r'[.!?]$', title)) or len(words) > 12
    generic_only = bool(re.fullmatch(r'(home|page|document|untitled|new page|welcome)', title, re.I))
    if sentence_like or generic_only or len(title) < 3:
        return [{'reason': 'unclear page title'}]
    return []

import re


def check_rule(text: str):
    lines = [ln.strip() for ln in text.splitlines() if ln.strip()]
    numbered_steps = sum(1 for ln in lines if re.match(r'^\d+[.)]\s+\S', ln))
    bullets = sum(1 for ln in lines if re.match(r'^[-*+]\s+\S', ln))
    imperative_lines = sum(1 for ln in lines if re.match(r'^(?:open|click|select|choose|enter|type|submit|save|review|check|confirm|download|upload|start|stop|install|remove|add|go to|use|make sure|ensure)\b', ln, re.I))

    if numbered_steps >= 2 or bullets >= 2:
        return [{'pattern': 'list-based instructions'}]
    if imperative_lines >= 2:
        return [{'pattern': 'imperative instructions'}]
    return []

import re

def check_rule(text: str):
    lines = [ln.strip() for ln in text.splitlines() if ln.strip()]
    findings = []
    step_patterns = [re.compile(r'^(?:\d+[.)]|[-*+])\s+')]
    for line in lines:
        is_step = any(p.match(line) for p in step_patterns)
        word_count = len(re.findall(r"\b\w+(?:'\w+)?\b", line))
        clause_count = len(re.findall(r',|\band\b|\bthen\b|\bnext\b|\bfinally\b', line, flags=re.IGNORECASE))
        if is_step and (word_count > 20 or clause_count >= 4):
            findings.append(line)
        elif not is_step and (word_count > 30 or clause_count >= 5):
            findings.append(line)
    return findings

import re

def check_rule(text: str):
    lines = [ln.rstrip() for ln in text.splitlines()]
    nonempty = [ln for ln in lines if ln.strip()]
    if not nonempty:
        return []
    heading_lines = [ln for ln in nonempty if re.match(r'^(#{1,6}\s+|[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9 ,:/()\-]{2,}$)', ln.strip())]
    list_lines = [ln for ln in nonempty if re.match(r'^(?:\d+[.)]|[-*+])\s+', ln.strip())]
    total_words = len(re.findall(r"\b\w+(?:'\w+)?\b", text))
    sentence_count = max(1, len(re.findall(r'[.!?]+', text)))
    avg_sentence_len = total_words / sentence_count
    if total_words >= 35 and len(nonempty) == 1 and len(heading_lines) == 0 and len(list_lines) == 0:
        return ['insufficient structure']
    if total_words >= 80 and len(heading_lines) == 0 and len(list_lines) == 0:
        return ['insufficient structure']
    if total_words >= 120 and avg_sentence_len > 20 and len(heading_lines) + len(list_lines) < 2:
        return ['insufficient structure']
    return []

trigger_code:
import re


def check_rule(text: str):
    lines = text.splitlines()
    findings = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        line = lines[i].strip()
        if '|' in line and re.search(r'\|\s*:?[-]{3,}', line):
            table_lines = [line]
            j = i + 1
            while j < len(lines) and ('|' in lines[j] or not lines[j].strip()):
                if lines[j].strip():
                    table_lines.append(lines[j].strip())
                j += 1
            rows = [re.split(r'(?<!\\)\|', tl.strip().strip('|')) for tl in table_lines if '|' in tl]
            rows = [[c.strip() for c in row] for row in rows if len(row) > 1]
            if rows:
                header = rows[0]
                ncols = len(header)
                max_cells = max((len(r) for r in rows), default=0)
                long_cell = any(len(c) > 80 for r in rows for c in r)
                if ncols > 6 or max_cells > 8 or long_cell:
                    findings.append({'table_start': i + 1, 'reason': 'table may be hard to scan'})
            i = j
        else:
            i += 1
    return findings

rule_summary: Check whether your writing has tics that annoy, distract or weaken readers' understanding.
rule_detail:
They’re the style habits we pick up and use unconsciously when writing. Granted, they can put the ‘you’ into writing and save it from being drearily bland. But it’s also possible your tics will:

- annoy and distract readers
- make the writing repetitive
- add redundant words
- get in the way of your message.
method_notes: Detecting distracting writing tics requires holistic judgement about style, repetition, redundancy, and reader impact. The same phrasing may be harmless in one context but annoying or weakening in another, so this cannot be reliably reduced to patterns or word lists.

trigger_code:
import re

def check_rule(text: str, lookup_list: list[str]):
    text_lower = text.lower()
    patterns = [
        r'\b(acronyms?|abbreviations?)\b.*\b(long forms?|full names?)\b',

    ]
    return [text] if any(re.search(pattern, text_lower) for pattern in patterns) else []

import re

def check_rule(text: str, lookup_list: list[str] | None = None):
    if lookup_list is None:
        lookup_list = [
            'please',
            'help you',
            'support you',
            'empower',
            'empowering',
            'designed to help',
            'designed to empower',
            'we are here to support you'
        ]

    found = []
    text_lower = text.lower()
    for term in lookup_list:
        pattern = r'\b' + re.escape(term.lower()) + r'\b'
        if re.search(pattern, text_lower):
            found.append(term)
    return found

trigger_code:
import re


def check_rule(text: str):
    blocks = [b.strip() for b in re.split(r'\n\s*\n+', text.strip()) if b.strip()]
    if not blocks:
        return []
    first = blocks[0]
    first_lower = first.lower()

    cues = [
        r'\b(summary|overview|purpose|key point|main point|in this document|this document|the purpose of|we (?:need|aim) to|you will|this letter|this email)\b',
        r'\b(action required|please|request|decision|recommendation|important|key information)\b'
    ]
    if any(re.search(p, first_lower) for p in cues):
        return []

    # Fire if a summary-like or key-information paragraph appears later, but not in the first block.
    later = '\n\n'.join(blocks[1:]).lower()
    if re.search(r'\b(summary|overview|purpose|key point|main point|in this document|this document|the purpose of|action required|decision|recommendation)\b', later):
        return ['Key information appears after the opening paragraph.']
    return []

trigger_code:
import re


def check_rule(text: str):
    lines = [ln.rstrip() for ln in text.splitlines()]
    subject_idx = None
    subject = ''
    for i, ln in enumerate(lines):
        m = re.match(r'^\s*subject\s*:\s*(.*)$', ln, re.I)
        if m:
            subject_idx = i
            subject = m.group(1).strip()
            break
    if subject_idx is None:
        return []

    subject_lower = subject.lower()
    if not subject or len(subject.split()) <= 2:
        # Very short/empty subjects are likely non-summaries.
        return ['Subject line does not summarise what is needed.']

    vague = re.search(r'\b(fyi|update|question|request|meeting|info|urgent|re\s*:)\b', subject_lower)
    has_specificity = re.search(r'\b(approval|approve|review|sign|sign-off|decision|comments|feedback|draft|attachment|budget|invoice|report|proposal|meeting notes|action required|deadline|response)\b', subject_lower)

    # If subject is vague and body has more detail, flag it.
    body = '\n'.join(lines[subject_idx + 1:]).lower()
    body_has_action = re.search(r'\b(please|action required|approve|review|sign|decision|feedback|response|by\s+\w+)\b', body)
    if (vague and not has_specificity) or (not has_specificity and body_has_action):
        return ['Subject line should summarise what is needed.']
    return []

trigger_code:
import re


def check_rule(text: str):
    blocks = [b.strip() for b in re.split(r'\n\s*\n+', text.strip()) if b.strip()]
    if len(blocks) < 3:
        return []

    beginning_pat = r'\b(beginning|start|initially|originally|before|current state|existing state|problem|issue|what we want to change)\b'
    middle_pat = r'\b(then|next|after|after that|during|event|step|process|change|transform|action|actions|move to|followed by)\b'
    end_pat = r'\b(end|end state|finally|lastly|final|result|outcome|desired outcome|new state|goal achieved|success|conclusion)\b'

    labels = []
    for block in blocks:
        b = block.lower()
        kinds = set()
        if re.search(beginning_pat, b):
            kinds.add('beginning')
        if re.search(middle_pat, b):
            kinds.add('middle')
        if re.search(end_pat, b):
            kinds.add('end')
        labels.append(kinds)

    has_beginning = any('beginning' in k for k in labels)
    has_middle = any('middle' in k for k in labels)
    has_end = any('end' in k for k in labels)

    if not (has_beginning and has_middle and has_end):
        return []

    first_beginning = next(i for i, k in enumerate(labels) if 'beginning' in k)
    first_middle = next(i for i, k in enumerate(labels) if 'middle' in k)
    first_end = next(i for i, k in enumerate(labels) if 'end' in k)

    if first_beginning < first_middle < first_end:
        return []

    if 'end' in labels[0]:
        return ['Beginning-middle-end structure appears out of order.']
    return ['Beginning-middle-end structure is incomplete or out of order.']

rule_summary: Prefer simple sentences with one idea when possible.
rule_detail: Simple sentences contain one idea. Complex sentences have one idea and extra information that contributes to that idea.
error_log: SHOULD fire but didn't: 'The team reviewed the draft and updated the appendix because several references were outdated and the examples were unclear.'
method_notes: Heuristic complexity check based on sentence length and presence of common coordination/subordination markers. Flags sentences that appear to contain multiple ideas. This is a proxy only; complex but acceptable sentences may be flagged, and some simple sentences may be missed.
trigger_code:
import re


def check_rule(text: str):
    findings = []
    sentence_split = re.compile(r'(?<=[.!?])\s+')
    sentences = [s.strip() for s in sentence_split.split(text.strip()) if s.strip()]
    multi_idea_markers = re.compile(r'\b(?:and|but|or|because|although|though|while|whereas|if|unless|when|since|after|before|however|therefore|which|that|who|whom|whose)\b', re.I)
    for s in sentences:
        words = s.split()
        if len(words) >= 20 and multi_idea_markers.search(s):
            findings.append(s)
    return findings

trigger_code:
import re


def check_rule(text: str):
    low = text.lower()
    has_technical_terms = len(re.findall(r'\b(?:api|algorithm|authentication|authorisation|authorization|database|metadata|parameter|protocol|schema|token|encryption|decryption|checksum|interface|configuration|deployment|repository|namespace|endpoint|serialization|deserialization)\b', low)) >= 3
    has_glossary = bool(re.search(r'(?im)^\s*#{0,6}\s*(glossary|terms|definitions)\s*$', text)) or 'glossary' in low
    if has_technical_terms and not has_glossary:
        return [{'issue': 'missing_glossary'}]
    return []

import re

def check_rule(text: str):
    # Heuristic: flag documents that look complicated/technical but lack glossary-like support.
    lower = text.lower()
    lines = [ln.strip() for ln in text.splitlines()]
    nonempty = [ln for ln in lines if ln]

    # Detect glossary/summary/support sections.
    glossary_markers = [
        r'^(#{1,6}\s*)?glossary\b',
        r'^(#{1,6}\s*)?definitions\b',
        r'^(#{1,6}\s*)?plain language summary\b',
        r'^(#{1,6}\s*)?summary\b',
    ]
    has_support_section = any(re.search(p, lower, re.M) for p in glossary_markers)

    # Heuristic technical complexity markers.
    technical_markers = [
        r'\bAPI\b', r'\bXML\b', r'\bJSON\b', r'\bCLI\b', r'\bSQL\b',
        r'\balgorithm\b', r'\bprocedure\b', r'\bconfiguration\b', r'\bparameter\b',
        r'\bimplementation\b', r'\bauthentication\b', r'\bencryption\b', r'\bcompliance\b'
    ]
    technical_hits = sum(bool(re.search(p, text, re.I)) for p in technical_markers)

    # Heuristic for long/complicated structure.
    headings = sum(1 for ln in lines if re.match(r'^(#{1,6}\s+|[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9 ,/-]{2,}:\s*$)', ln))
    bullets = sum(1 for ln in lines if re.match(r'^\s*([-*+]\s+|\d+[.)]\s+)', ln))
    long_paragraphs = [p for p in re.split(r'\n\s*\n', text) if len(p.split()) >= 120]
    complexity_score = technical_hits + (1 if headings >= 3 else 0) + (1 if bullets >= 5 else 0) + (1 if len(long_paragraphs) >= 2 else 0)

    if complexity_score >= 2 and not has_support_section:
        return [{'issue': 'complicated content without glossary/support section'}]
    return []

import re

def check_rule(text: str, lookup_list: list[str]):
    text_lower = text.lower()
    has_if = re.search(r'\bif\b', text_lower) is not None
    has_unless = re.search(r'\bunless\b', text_lower) is not None
    if has_if and has_unless:
        return ['if', 'unless']
    return []

method_notes: Whole-word, case-insensitive matching. This rule is broad and best implemented as a set of search/SEO-related keyword terms.
trigger_code:
import re

def check_rule(text: str, lookup_list: list[str]):
    text_lower = text.lower()
    patterns = [
        r'\bsearch\s+terms?\b',
        r'\bsearch\s+query\b',
        r'\bsearch\s+queries\b',
        r'\bkeyword\b',
        r'\bkeywords\b'
    ]
    found = []
    for pattern in patterns:
        match = re.search(pattern, text_lower)
        if match:
            found.append(match.group(0))
    return found

trigger_code:
import re

def check_rule(text: str):
    findings = []
    has_heading = bool(re.search(r'(?m)^\s*#{1,6}\s+\S', text))
    has_image_alt = bool(re.search(r'!\[[^\]]+\]\([^\)]+\)', text))
    text_wo_images = re.sub(r'!\[[^\]]*\]\([^\)]+\)', '', text)
    has_link = bool(re.search(r'\[[^\]]+\]\([^\)]+\)', text_wo_images)) or bool(re.search(r'(?i)\bhttps?://\S+', text_wo_images))
    has_metadata = bool(re.search(r'(?m)^\s*(title|description|keywords|meta[- ]?description)\s*:\s*\S.+$', text, re.I)) or bool(re.search(r'(?sm)^---\s*.*?^\s*(title|description|keywords)\s*:\s*\S.+?^---\s*$', text, re.I | re.M))
    has_page_content = bool(text.strip())
    if not has_page_content:
        return []
    if has_metadata and has_heading and has_link and has_image_alt:
        findings.append('page content uses keywords across metadata, headings, links, and image alt text')
    return findings

rule_summary: Use an initial capital when writing about protective markings in general content.
rule_detail: In general content, use an initial capital unless you are reporting how the protective marking actually appears on the page.
method_notes: Uses a simple text heuristic: flags lowercase occurrences of protective marking terms in running text when they are not inside quotation marks. This cannot distinguish discussion of typography from quoted reproduction in all cases.
trigger_code:
import re

MARKINGS = [
    'official', 'official:sensitive', 'protected', 'protected:government',
    'protected:commercial', 'protected:law enforcement', 'protected:security',
    'confidential', 'secret', 'top secret', 'cabinet', 'in confidence'
]

pattern = re.compile(r'\b(' + '|'.join(re.escape(m) for m in sorted(MARKINGS, key=len, reverse=True)) + r')\b')

quote_pairs = [('"', '"'), ('\u201c', '\u201d'), ("'", "'"), ('\u2018', '\u2019')]

def _in_quotes(text, start):
    open_pos = -1
    open_char = None
    close_char = None
    for a, b in quote_pairs:
        p = text.rfind(a, 0, start)
        if p > open_pos:
            open_pos = p
            open_char = a
            close_char = b
    if open_pos == -1:
        return False
    close_pos = text.find(close_char, open_pos + 1)
    return close_pos != -1 and close_pos > start


def check_rule(text: str):
    findings = []
    text_lower = text.lower()
    for m in pattern.finditer(text_lower):
        matched_text = text[m.start():m.end()]
        if matched_text[:1].islower() and not _in_quotes(text, m.start()):
            findings.append(matched_text)
    return findings

trigger_code:
import re

MARKINGS = [
    'official', 'official:sensitive', 'protected', 'protected:government',
    'protected:commercial', 'protected:law enforcement', 'protected:security',
    'confidential', 'secret', 'top secret', 'cabinet', 'in confidence'
]

pattern = re.compile(r'\b(' + '|'.join(re.escape(m) for m in sorted(MARKINGS, key=len, reverse=True)) + r')\b', re.I)
quote_patterns = [
    re.compile(r'"([^"]*?)"'),
    re.compile(r'“([^”]*?)”'),
    re.compile(r"'([^']*?)'"),
    re.compile(r'‘([^’]*?)’')
]

def check_rule(text: str):
    findings = []
    for qp in quote_patterns:
        for m in qp.finditer(text):
            inner = m.group(1)
            for mark in pattern.finditer(inner):
                word = mark.group(1)
                if word != word.upper():
                    findings.append(m.group(0))
                    break
    return findings
